measurement_notes: Fresh condition-level subagent context, no other condition answers/results read. Cases interleaved/batched within one context using expected_evidence file hints. elapsed_seconds is summed instrumented tool duration, not end-to-end per-case task latency; do not compare as speed advantage. Token estimates ceil((prompt + tool arguments + canonical tool text chars)/4) and ceil(answer chars/4), excluding system/history/reasoning/caching/wrapper duplication. Not actual telemetry. Setup excludes initial skill/tool discovery and AGENTS/case/schema read, timed from post-schema setup marker through health; no indexing performed. See mcp-measurement-notes.md and mcp-evidence-log.json.

runs.answer: Imports _mcp's shared stateful FastMCP instance, which loads environment and calls register_all for brain/hands tools. brain_server creates the MCP Starlette app, mounts it at root so /mcp remains intact, and exposes / and /health plus /fingerprint before the mount. Direct execution starts uvicorn at 127.0.0.1:8001. Health reports protocol versions, tool count, boot/fingerprint, uptime and session state.

runs.answer: _persist_job_state serializes runtime fields including statuses, return codes, PIDs, log paths, timestamps and maintenance state to a unique temporary JSON file then atomically replaces state. load_job_record checks memory then disk, reconciles running/cancelling records and restores them to the registry. Reconciliation polls surviving Popen objects; for dead recorded PIDs it infers return codes from logs or marks failure. Once both phases finish it sets done/failed/cancelled, records finish time, removes manifest, releases project/capacity locks, persists, and runs pending post-index maintenance.

runs.answer: search_codebase_core resolves workspace IDs, classifies implementation intent/identifiers/path hints, and gathers project searches. SQL ranks vector neighbors and keyword hits with weighted RRF (2/(60+semantic rank) plus 1/(60+keyword rank)); the left join is anchored in semantic candidates. It rescues explicit runtime/path definitions, filters metadata/path/test/crate scope, enriches implementation scores through retrieval_policy/retrieval_scoring, penalizes low-signal/doc surfaces and sorts candidates. It can rescue definitions/member usages through grep and load matching indexed rows, apply optional clone dedup, duplicate/file postprocessing, then per-file/directory caps and top-k. Broad mode relaxes caps and enables grep; concentrated final results can emit exact grep fallback paths.

runs.answer: indexer.py delegates to index_docs. The pipeline opens/bootstrap storage and probes embeddings before crawling. Discovery is opt-in; discover_pages tries llms.txt and sitemap/link discovery with scope/filter handling. Without discovery, deduplicated seeds are used. crawl_pages treats raw GitHub markdown directly and uses adaptive HTTP/Playwright plus trafilatura for other content. chunk_content prefers ts_pack markdown/XML AST chunks and context paths, with line-window fallback. index_docs buffers chunks, embeds at effective batch size, and upserts doc_embeddings by chunk_id, including content, vector and metadata (topic/title/context/domain/type/section). Storage errors return zero written.

runs.answer: get_symbol_context is registered in tools/brain/code_intel/core.py. It obtains the project-scoped graph candidate query, normalizes file/signature filters, and uses symbol_graph helpers to disambiguate or rank/select a candidate and format definition/call relationships. No candidate returns a not-found message; a graph failure returns an error rather than bypassing graph lookup. For source preview it prefers local disk at the graph symbol span with line/character caps; if unavailable it queries Postgres by project/file, prioritizing declared symbol, definition chunk role and proximity to start_line. Preview failures are swallowed so graph context can still return.

runs.answer: get_test_coverage_for combines filesystem name patterns (Python/TS/Rust/Go), Neo4j IMPORTS and IMPORTS_SYMBOL edges, and ripgrep basename mentions in test files. If no matches, it tries generic route suites/route token matches and then project-scoped Postgres test/spec chunks containing path/basename tokens, filtered by file roles. It deduplicates by file, favors package locality and stronger match reasons, limits weak basename matches, and returns up to 25. Graph/text/semantic errors are guarded. These are likely related tests, not measured execution coverage.

runs.answer: _mcp configures stateful HTTP (stateless_http=False), so transport sessions belong to the current process. brain_server generates a new PID/UUID BOOT_ID and checks the incoming mcp-session-id against session_manager._server_instances for diagnostic known/active values. Middleware delegates protocol handling to the MCP app; when its response is 404 for a supplied session ID it logs a stale rejection once. It attaches boot/fingerprint/session-known headers, and health exposes the snapshot. BOOT_ID is diagnostic, not a middleware comparison that itself rejects the request.

runs.answer: compute_tool_fingerprint hashes sorted registered tool names plus source path/content SHA256 records and returns a 12-hex prefix and tool count. Sources include inspected tool function files, recursive Python files in tools/graphrag_core/memory/local_embeddings, listed Python helpers, and explicit runtime_source_files such as brain_server.py. Unreadable files get a sentinel. Although requirements.txt and requirements-ci.txt are listed in default roots, the file collector only accepts .py files, so dependency-pin changes in those text manifests do not affect the default fingerprint. Installed dependency versions/content are not directly hashed.

runs.answer: trace_symbol_cross_project_core resolves source and target workspace IDs/paths. It queries source-project named definitions and export aliases, selects the highest _definition_rank candidate, and expands resolved names for aliases. Target graph consumers are callers in the target project with CALLS/CALLS_INFERRED to named symbols; target matching itself is by name rather than source project. Semantic consumers combine target-project exact text and vector/keyword candidates, require symbol text, dedupe chunk keys, rank using _semantic_usage_rank and keep one hit per file up to five. Source previews are selected near the chosen definition. Output distinguishes structural consumers, implementation text and test/support text.
